extracted.intended_audience: scholars, students, and general readers interested in political communication, public opinion, and media effects
extracted.subtask_description: A publisher product page describing an academic book (News That Matters) about television news effects on public opinion, summarizing findings, chapters, and reviewer praise. Targets readers evaluating the book's contribution and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hypotheses articulation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the Journal of Communication review: 'The book is in many ways a model of research reporting. Hypotheses are expressly articulated...' (used as a positive standard for research reporting—clear statement of hypotheses is a mark of quality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodology transparency
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers praise the book because its methodology is carefully detailed; the book reports 'ingenious experiments' that unobtrusively altered the order and emphasis of news stories in selected television broadcasts, demonstrating how to design and report experiments that identify media effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data presentation and explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Data clearly presented and convincingly explained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Journal of Communication review notes 'data clearly presented and, best of all often convincingly explained.' The book also uses careful analysis of public opinion surveys to back experimental findings—clear display and interpretation of data is treated as a core quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental design quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a complex, integrated, and ingenious system of experiments to test media effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice review: 'The authors have put together a complex, integrated system of experiments testing the effects of television news that is equal to the complexity of the process by which viewers comprehend such information.' High-quality work uses multiple, well-integrated experiments that match the cognitive processes under study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence for agenda-setting and priming effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Issues that receive extended coverage become more important to viewers; prominent issues influence presidential evaluations and candidate choice (agenda-setting and priming effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Book summary: 'those issues that receive extended coverage in the national news become more important to viewers... those issues that are prominent in the news stream continue to loom more heavily as criteria for evaluating the president and for choosing between political candidates.' This substantive finding is presented as the central empirical claim and standard of relevance for the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cautious presentation of conclusions and readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions are carefully and cautiously presented and written in a lucid, readable manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choice review praises the book for cautious presentation: '...The conclusions are carefully and cautiously presented, making it one of the most readable works of experimental research.' Readability and restraint in claims are thus highlighted as qualities of strong scholarship.
